correctness.rationale: Frisch--Waugh--Lovell reduces the mirror pair to orthogonal residualized columns because the published normalization equalizes their component norms. This gives the independent normal coefficient laws exactly. The mirror identity is elementary; the alternative sign probability follows by standardization. Strict monotonicity is proved by the increasing function H(x)=x[2Phi(x)-1]/phi(x). Uniform-sphere geometry gives the rho density and exact moments, yielding the mixture and fixed-lambda expansion. Deterministic replay in verify.py matches all displayed numerical examples. Limits are explicit: low-dimensional fixed-design Gaussian OLS only, and sign probability is not full procedure power.

value.rationale: The published method intentionally randomizes each feature and emphasizes statistical power. Near the p<n boundary, residual dimension d=n-p+1 is small, and the exact law shows a material featurewise sign-gate loss from the random perturbation direction. This is a natural finite-sample diagnostic of the method, supplies explicit benchmarks for implementation/simulation, and identifies a mathematically motivated design coordinate without claiming a replacement procedure or a global power theorem.
